best_for: Students, analysts and researchers who write R on a Windows 11 PC or a recent Mac and want the editor, console, plots and data viewer in one window.
description:
RStudio is a development environment for the R language, made by Posit Software. You write code, explore data and share results in one window. Posit says it believes data science software should be free and open for everyone, and it also makes Positron, a newer editor for both R and Python.

You can run code line by line or all at once, fold code, jump to a function, and follow a document outline. The Environment pane lists every object in your session, histogram filters narrow a big data frame by sight, and the Connections pane links to your databases. SQL is supported alongside R. When the work is done, you can publish Shiny apps, reports and dashboards to Posit Connect, shinyapps.io or RPubs right from the IDE.

points.title: Install R first
points.text: RStudio does not include R. Posit's download page says you need a separate R installation, which most computers do not have, and that on Windows nothing else is needed once R is in place.

points.title: Free under the AGPL
points.text: The open source edition costs nothing and is licensed under AGPL v3, with help through the community forum. Organizations that cannot use AGPL software can buy RStudio Desktop Pro, listed at USD 1,204 per year with priority email support and Posit's database drivers. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Built for R, not only R
points.text: The editor has completion and diagnostics for R, a data viewer with sorting and filters, a debugger, Git, projects and package tools. Python runs through the reticulate package, and Quarto and R Markdown documents get a visual editor.

points.title: AI help is a paid add-on
points.text: Posit sells an AI add-on for USD 20 per month that works with any edition, with a free trial that asks for no credit card. The base IDE works without it.

points.title: Newer systems only
points.text: Posit lists Windows 11 and macOS 15 or later for the current release. The Mac download is a single universal build for Apple silicon and Intel. Windows gets 64-bit builds only, as a per-user or machine-wide installer.

points.title: Linux is official but not listed here
points.text: Posit offers .deb packages for Ubuntu and Debian and .rpm packages for RHEL and Fedora, for x86_64 only. This site lists Windows and macOS builds.

points.title: Older versions on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 54 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so a Mac downgrade needs another source.
